 Dream vs. Valkyries live updates: Angel Reese, Atlanta looking for commanding WNBA Finals lead
 The Dream have a chance to take a 3-1 series lead in Game 4 of the 2026 WNBA Finals on Saturday afternoon
 By
 Jack Maloney 
  &
 Lindsay Gibbs 
 Oct 24, 2026
 at
 2:15 pm ET 
 •
 1 min read
 Add CBS Sports on Google 
 Join the Conversation
 comments 
 It's Game 4 of the 2026 WNBA Finals on Saturday afternoon as the Atlanta Dream host the Golden State Valkyries. Atlanta has won two straight games to take a 2-1 series lead and has the chance to take a commanding advantage in the best-of-seven matchup on Saturday at State Farm Arena.
 Angel Reese is the heavy WNBA Finals favorite after having back-to-back stellar games. Reese has combined for 51 points and 28 rebounds in the last two games, shooting a combined 17 for 28 from the floor while hitting all three of the 3-pointers she's attempted.
 The Valkyries, who had the WNBA's best defense this season, need to come up with an answer for Reese, and they need to find some scoring of their own. Golden State is averaging just 68 points per game in the Finals.
 Dream vs. Valkyries: WNBA Finals Game 4
 Time : 1 p.m. ET | Date : Saturday, Oct. 24
 Location : State Farm Arena -- Atlanta
 TV channel : NBC | Live stream :  fubo  (Try for free)
 Odds (via DraftKings): ATL -4.5 | O/U: 153.5
 Will the Dream take a commanding 3-1 series lead? Or will the Valkyries even things up on the road? CBS Sports will have live updates and analysis throughout Game 4. Follow along below.

 Halftime: Valkyries 42 -- Dream 26
 The Valkyries dominated the second quarter to take a 16-point lead into the break, and are 20 minutes away from evening up this series. Their defense has been dominant. They've forced 13 Dream turnovers, which they've turned into 16 points, and have held the Dream to just 26 points. 
 Between the turnovers they've forced and their efforts on the offensive glass (eight offensive rebounds), the Valkyries have taken a staggering 21 more shots than the Dream already. That's why they're up big even though the two teams are shooting an almost identical percentage: 42.5% for the Valkyries, 42.1% for the Dream

 Valkyries on 9-0 run to take biggest lead of series
 The Valkyries are on a 9-0 run late in the second half that has pushed their lead up to 13 -- their biggest advantage of the entire series. Their activity and physicality on the defensive end has the Dream all out of sorts. Atlanta has already turned it over 10 times and still only has 20 points as we approach halftime

 Reese finally gets on the board
 Angel Reese has been out of sorts today, particularly on the offensive end, but just got on the board with a little hook shot in the paint. We'll see if that can get her going. The Dream have really relied on her scoring throughout this run, but she has more turnovers (three) than points (two) right now

 First quarter: Valkyries 16 -- Dream 11
 The Valkyries came out with a new starting lineup and the desperation of a team facing a 2-1 deficit in the Finals. Offense has still been hard to come by for Golden State, but their energy and physicality has overwhelmed Atlanta on both ends. The Valkyries are only 7 of 22 (31.8%), but they've taken 12 more shots than the Dream thanks to five offensive rebounds and seven Dream turnovers. 
 Kaila Charles, inserted into the starting lineup, has five points, three rebounds and an assist, while Cecilia Zandalasni, who ceded her spot to Charles, has come off the bench to score five points as well. 
 Allisha Gray picked up three fouls in the first quarter and only has two points, while Angel Reese was scoreless in the first.

 Another low-scoring start
 It's 7-4 Dream at the first TV timeout in what has been another low-scoring start in these Finals. The Dream are 2 of 6 from the field, while the Valkyries are 2 of 12. The Valkyries' lineup change hasn't provided the offensive boost they were hoping for, but they have at least generated some decent looks

 Valkyries switching up the starting lineup
 Natalie Nakase has made a big move with her team down 2-1 in the Finals. Tiffany Hayes and Kaila Charles have been inserted into the starting lineup in place of Kayla Thornton and Cecilia Zandalasini. 
 Hayes is one of the few Golden State players who can reliably create their own shot, and has been in double digits off the bench in each of the last two games, while Charles was stellar in Game 1 and brings a pop of energy and athleticism.
